summary: Remote WebSocket peer drives PTY, filesystem, and self-upgrade on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a long-lived agent that connects to a WebSocket server (SERVER_URL, configurable; default ws://localhost:3456 but designed for remote operation per the package's 'Remote worker agent' description) and dispatches inbound messages to privileged local handlers. terminal.js spawns an interactive PTY via pty.spawn(process.env.SHELL || 'bash',...) on `terminal_create` frames, and message-router.js writes raw peer bytes into that PTY via term.pty.write(msg.data) on `terminal_input` frames received from socket.on('message',...) in connection/index.js. Additional message types expose arbitrary file read/write, git operations, an npm-based self-upgrade of the agent, and localhost HTTP/WS proxying. Any party that controls or reaches the configured WebSocket server obtains full interactive shell and filesystem access on the host running the agent, plus the ability to replace the agent binary in place. service/linux.js also modifies the user's PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of the service install.
